note: 2026-10-11 daily batch. WRITTEN BY THE RESEARCH ANALYST AT ZERO RETRIEVAL COST as the seat's ruling on the one relay slot, after the chairman's mid-session evidence hand-off. THE CHAIRMAN'S THREE QUESTIONS, RULED ON. (1) HIS DATE-LITERAL PREMISE IS CONFIRMED and this seat corroborated it independently and added prior art he did not have: a date literal of the form 'Month D, YYYY' is attested as a matching find on icsid.worldbank.org in TWO prior rows - 'January 29, 2025' (2026-09-13-zz-docket-chronology.json idx 1, find_matched TRUE, 98122 bytes, sha da8b441f) and 'April 13, 2026' (2026-09-16-daily.json idx 1, find_matched TRUE, same page, sha 8020e794). Per the prior-art screen adopted 2026-10-07 (open_threads[0-based 51]) the instrument claim 'date literals are usable finds on this host' is NOT NOVEL; what is new below is their first use on /cases/recent, where 0 of 586 prior rows carry a date-shaped find. (2) HIS POINT 2 IS PARTLY SUSTAINED AND PARTLY CORRECTED, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS. Sustained: the head window does already name the top of the table, so re-reading the SAME REGION would be the failure 2026-10-09 struck. Corrected in two ways. (2a) A DATE-LITERAL ROW IS A PAGE-WIDE PROBE, NOT A HEAD-OF-TABLE PROBE: excerpt_of searches the WHOLE tag-stripped body (scripts/fetch_relay.py:131, body.lower().find(find.lower())) before any window is cut, so a null on a date literal is absence of that literal from the ENTIRE 363-kilobyte rendering and does not depend on the monotonic-ordering premise at all. On a 363,110-byte page whose head window shows only four entries, that is a strictly different and stronger epistemic product than reading the excerpt, and it is why date rows survive below. (2b) HIS 'EXACTLY TWO ENTRIES' IS THE UPPER BOUND OF A RANGE, NOT A FINDING, AND THE ARITHMETIC SHOWS WHY. This seat counted the characters. The first 100 characters of the idx-5 excerpt are exactly 'd Published Concluded Constituted October 6, 2026 Lombard North Central PLC v. Republic of Turkiye (' - 100 characters on the nose, and excerpt_of cuts at idx - EXCERPT_CHARS // 4 = idx - 100 (scripts/fetch_relay.py:42, :134). So the FIRST occurrence of 'ICSID Case No.' on that page is Lombard's, LOMBARD IS THE FIRST DATA ENTRY, and nothing stands between 'Constituted' and 'October 6, 2026' or between that date and 'Lombard' except one space each. Therefore: if the rendering puts each entry's date BEFORE its name, the leading date binds to Lombard, the second Oct 6 binds to Sopam, and TWO entries fall inside 2026-09-28..2026-10-10; if the rendering puts the date AFTER the name, the leading date belongs to no entry at all (it is header or stamp text), Lombard is Oct 6, Sopam is Sep 23, and ONE entry falls inside the window. ONE OR TWO. The record's 'two ICSID entries dated October 6, 2026' and today's agenda's 'the window is not quiet at the source' are both written at the top of that range, and this request does not adopt either. (3) ON COLUMN SEMANTICS - HIS QUESTION IS THE RIGHT ONE, AND IT IS NOT ANSWERABLE ON /cases/recent BY THIS INSTRUMENT, EVER. The tag-strip removes script and style bodies and then every remaining tag and collapses whitespace (scripts/fetch_relay.py:78-80, :126-128) BEFORE the search runs, so a cell boundary and a space inside one cell render identically. No find on that page can bind a date to a column, and no number of windows will change that: the information is destroyed upstream of the search. BUT THE QUESTION IS ANSWERABLE ON A DIFFERENT PAGE OF THE SAME HOST, AND THE CORPUS PROVES IT. ICSID's case-detail pages carry LABELLED prose, and 28 of 28 prior rows with find 'Subject of Dispute' on case-detail URLs returned find_matched TRUE - including THREE ARB/26/xx pages. 2026-09-18-daily.json idx 1 (ARB/26/36) returned verbatim 'Subject of Dispute: Mining concession Economic Sector: Oil, Gas & Mining Instrument(s) Invoked: (i) BIT United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland - Mexico 2006 Applicable Rules: ICSID'; idx 3 (ARB/26/38) returned 'Subject of Dispute: Oil production enterprise Economic Sector: Oil & Gas Instrument(s) Invoked: (i) BIT Spain - Argentina 1991'. And the companion literal 'Status of Proceeding' returned, on those same two pages, 'Status of Proceeding: Pending Latest Development: July 24, 2026 - The Secretary-General registers a request for the institution of arbitration proceedings' (ARB/26/36) and the same sentence at 'September 15, 2026' (ARB/26/38) - ICSID'S OWN LABELLED STATEMENT OF THE REGISTRATION EVENT AND ITS DATE. That is precisely the fact the chairman says is load-bearing, available in one window, on a page family where the label travels with the value. SO THE SLOT IS SPLIT 8/4: eight rows on /cases/recent (two controls, six page-wide date probes) and four rows across the two case-detail pages of the two matters the 2026-10-10 excerpt named. THE ONE QUESTION THIS BATCH NAMES: what, in ICSID's own labelled prose, are the two matters the 2026-10-10 relay surfaced adjacent to the collector's unsampled window - their status, their registration event and date, their subject of dispute, sector and instrument invoked - and does any other entry bearing an in-window date literal appear anywhere in the visible prose of /cases/recent? DATE SELECTION RULE, FIXED HERE AND CALENDAR-DERIVED SO IT IS NOT CHOOSABLE AFTER THE RESULT: take the Monday-to-Friday dates of 2026-09-28..2026-10-11 from the LATE end backward, as many as the slots allow. That yields October 9, 8, 7, 6, 5 and 2. UNFIRED AND EXPRESSLY UNFOUNDED: October 1 and September 30, 29 and 28 (business days, dropped for budget, not for any belief about them) and October 3, 4, 10 and 11 (the Saturdays and Sundays of the window by the civil calendar - a calendar fact, NOT a claim about when ICSID registers anything). THE BATCH FOUNDS NOTHING WHATEVER ABOUT THOSE EIGHT DATES. WHAT A DATE NULL FOUNDS, BINDING: absence of that exact literal from the tag-stripped, whitespace-collapsed rendering at the batch instant, given that the two same-URL controls hit. It is NOT a finding that no ICSID case was registered, constituted, concluded or published on that day; G16 bars a docket-summary surface from founding a disposition and the project's absence rule is 'not found in accessible sources'. The find is CASE-INSENSITIVE (:131), which widens every row, and it is FORM-SPECIFIC: a page rendering '6 October 2026' or 'Oct. 6, 2026' somewhere would not match, so a null is a null ON THIS FORM. OUTCOME CLASSES THAT ARE FACTS ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT AND MAY NEVER BE WRITTEN AS FINDINGS ABOUT ICSID OR ANY MATTER: control_ok false (whole batch VOID); refused / 403 / 202 / timeout / no_contact; host_not_allowed / scheme_not_https; a 404 or redirect on either case-detail URL, which is NEVER a statement that the case does not exist; a FALSE on rows 1 or 2, which would void the interpretation of all six date rows; and both rows on one case-detail URL missing together, which is UNINTERPRETABLE as to that page and goes back as an instrument observation, not as a statement about the matter. NO ORDINAL OR COUNT INFERENCE IS DRAWN OR AUTHORISED: that ARB/26/38 was registered 2026-09-15 and ARB/26/39 and ARB/26/40 carry higher ordinals is noted here as an INFERENCE ONLY and is not a finding; no seat may convert these rows into a registration count, a rate, or an ordinal fact. NO PDF ROW: find_matched is bool(find) and bool(excerpt_of(...)) at :181 and excerpt_of returns '' for any content type that is neither html nor text (:124), so a PDF can never return a relay TRUE and no row below is a PDF. THIS IS A WRITE ONLY: the workflow fires on the chairman's push, not on this file's existence, so no result lands inside this session. THIS BATCH DOES NOT TOUCH AND DOES NOT RE-ANCHOR ANY CADENCED CLOCK. It is NOT the ICSID Decisions on Manifest Lack of Legal Merit register row (open_threads[0-based 11]'s relay limb, due on or around 2026-10-13) and no row below goes near that URL. It is NOT the PCA register row (open_threads[0-based 39]), which this council's standing ruling says DO NOT FIRE IT EARLY. It is NOT the monthly standing watch on open_threads[0-based 10] / [0-based 25]: no row below carries 'Wingtech' or 'Yuching', and the /cases/recent rows here are date and control rows, not a Wingtech observation. STANDING PROHIBITIONS HONOURED: no www.italaw.com row and no bare italaw.com row; no investmentpolicy.unctad.org row and no bare unctad.org row; no ARB/24/16 row; no dailyjus.com row; no IISD path-family row; no www.bing.com row; no row touching open_threads[0-based] 2, 34, 42 or 43; and no gap-closing row beyond the one question named above.
